And to 1,344 / 1,279 with (30), THE NOTATION THAT CLOSES ON THE NEXT COLON. A § ... # states the reach of the bar inside it and the reach is Stipp's, not his colometry's: at 6,6 the § rides on the label of colon d, the bar stands in colon e and the # at its left edge, so read colon by colon the bar was bare, reached one word on each side, and the surplus of the ALEXANDRIAN reading stayed common - HOJ 'IR HA-SHEQER printed in the masoretic column where BHS has only HI' HA-'IR HAPQAD. THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING COMES DOWN 23 -> 19; 6,6, 20,11, 22,4, 33,2 and 44,12 are the five, and nothing else moved. The carry is bounded by a lookahead rather than by a threshold: a notation reaches only where the next colon puts a bar in it, which keeps it out of Stipp's OTHER notation, the marked stretch with no bar where the two editions have the same consonants and the difference is described in the note. Unbounded it empties the alexandrian cell, which no figure here can see - 21,8c, the book's one reversed pair, ran nine colons to 21,10c. And to 1,365 / 1,299 / 0.996 on 2026-09-10, on two readings that had nothing to do with the notation. (31) A PLUS THAT OPENS IN THE MARGIN. Stipp brackets a plus that wraps to the left end of a printed line; the closing bracket lands in the text column and the opening bracket and the bracketed word land beyond MARGIN_X, so the word was dropped and only its closer survived - LE'MOR at 26,11, BEN-SHAFAN at 43,6. The test is structural and uses no geometry, which is why it reaches where OVERFLOW_X cannot: twelve of these words sit at x = 30.2, where the margin's own lemmas also live. 19 printed lines of the book, 17 verses. Only a RAISED line may be stepped over; stepping over any line without Hebrew costs eleven verses and loses one from the book. THE EXTRA-TEXT CEILING COMES DOWN 19 -> 16.
